sources.interpretation: Leading-foundry profitability makes a 40% incremental merchant EBIT case economically conceivable, but does not validate it for Intel. TSMC scale, pricing, mix, mature utilization and local costs differ.

sources.facts: Overseas fabs dilute consolidated gross margin by approximately 2 percentage points in 2026 and 3–4 points in the next few years; 2026 capital budget is $60–64B; TSMC is adding capacity and converting N5 tools for N3.
sources.interpretation: Consolidated dilution is weighted by foreign revenue and does not mean Arizona itself costs only 2–4 margin points extra. Domestic geography is not an exclusive Intel advantage; competitors also reuse tools and add capacity.

option_boundary: Our $10B of 2033 merchant revenue is a normalized success scenario, not an awarded customer forecast. It is large relative to current non-TSMC players and requires multiple customers/programs, qualified capacity, retained margins and financing. Broad TAM or TSMC margin alone cannot establish its probability.
joint_case: Applying the independently selected maturing-risk curve to the previously frozen favorable wafer platform gives $4.200652424 per share, fully funded. The appropriate objection to a high-conviction short is the coherent combination of CPU value capture, capital productivity, risk maturation and merchant upside. The merchant-wafer option need not bridge the old flat-12% $78B gap alone.
